description: Player 1's deck for the Sheepish spec. Two cards carry the scenario and both cost one mana, so a single two-mana turn holds the whole sequence. #11 Tempo Timmy is the Unit whose play springs the trap: it has no Cry, so nothing about the transform can be confused with a Cry that fizzled, and it is not Immutable, which R17 and R23 would let refuse the Transform outright ("Sheepish on an Immutable unit still fires and is consumed with no effect"). #15 Me and Mr Token is the Unit played immediately afterwards: its Cry summons a Rush Token, so the token on the board is the proof that player 1 could continue and that the next play's Cry still fires (R118). The other eighteen are choice-free filler that keeps the deck legal and never opens a picker; nothing here is a Trap, a Cast-on-draw card or a Quickdraw card, so the only trap in the game is player 2's. No card here carries a start-of-turn, end-of-turn or on-play hook that acts on the board (#58 Rush Token Farm and #64 Gifted Program were removed for exactly that): `triggerHoldersWithHook` in packages/engine/src/triggers.ts gathers those hooks from the HAND as well as the field, so a Rush Token Farm sitting in hand summons a unit every turn and a Gifted Program in hand makes a cheap play Radiant - which would move the board and the stats this spec asserts. Reported as an engine finding; the fixture does not rely on it either way. Its seat plays under the handicap below, TUTORIAL_HUMAN's (R1705005): a human's resources with a deck of 20, the size every deck had before #1705, so these cards and the deal the spec's seed was tuned on stand. #5099: #8 Mr. Vanilla, #11 Tempo Timmy, #20 Pointmaster and #25 4-mana 7/7, a card whose whole text is its keyword line, are dealt as stand-ins (crates/engine/src/testkit/stand_in.rs) spelling their numbers as they stood, in the same place in the list, so the deal is unchanged and no balance patch moves them.
cards: stand-in (1) 3/3 Rush, First Strike R6/6 Charge, First Strike
